newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares climb, pushed up by Lek.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares climb, pushed up by Lek.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 1.59 percent on Tuesday, pulled up by a 7.42 percent surge in the A issue of drug company Lek, traders said.

"Foreign and domestic investors believe Lek's current price to be low as it is significantly below the 35,000 reached a week ago. Therefore Lek may continue to pull the market up until it reaches 35,000 again," one trader said.
Lek's A issue reached its 1996 high on February 28 when it rose to 35,500 tolars in the middle of the day but then eased to 32,200 by the end of the day.

"The market is also waiting for the listing of drug company Krka on Monday, which can be compared to Lek in size and in business performance -- a rise in Krka's shares may pull Lek further up," the trader added.
At the moment Krka is traded at between 14,000 and 20,000 tolars on the grey market.
The 11-share SBI index rose 24.84 percent to 1,583.7.
Overall 10 shares rose, six fell and nine were not traded. Turnover rose to 549 million tolars from 352.9 million.
Lek's A issue was the most actively traded and was the top gainer, rising to 30,400 tolars on volume of 10,191 shares for total turnover of 296.8 million tolars.
Pharmaceutival trader Salus was the leading decliner, closing 4.21 percent lower at 15,020 on volume of 200 shares for total turnover of 3.0 million tolars.
